task.title: Discover durable workflow runs from authoritative start events
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/697 under decision https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/696 by listing every valid workflow-run aggregate deterministically without maintaining a secondary index.
acceptance_criteria: Discover only streams containing the exact authoritative workflow_run.started event discriminator.
Project every candidate through the same strict complete-history function used by exact-ID loading.
Return active, authored-terminal, and cancelled aggregate state once each in ascending exact run-ID order.
Fail the complete listing without partial results when a candidate stream ID or history is malformed.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused workflow_run_store tests failed because WorkflowRunStore::list did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for complete mixed-state discovery, deterministic exact-ID ordering, unrelated-stream exclusion, reopen behavior, and fail-closed malformed candidate handling.

attempts.summary: Implemented authoritative full-history discovery with one shared projector.
attempts.diagnostic: Discovering from the immutable start discriminator avoided a second mutable index, while shared exact-ID projection prevented load and list replay semantics from drifting.
attempts.patch: Added event-log candidate-stream replay, strict stream-ID recovery, deterministic list projection, ADR-0012, and milestone documentation.

attempts.summary: Accepted the documented full-scan cost after substantive review.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit confirmed the implementation was correct and noted that listing cost grows with total candidate history because pagination, indexing, and caching were deliberately deferred.
attempts.patch: Kept the KISS full-scan boundary and recorded scaling as a trigger for a later measured pagination or indexing decision rather than adding speculative infrastructure.

outcome.summary: Callers can now recover every durable workflow run in deterministic order from authoritative event history with no secondary index or partial corrupt result.

lessons: An immutable authoritative start event can serve as the discovery index while the dataset remains small enough for full replay.
Exact loading and listing should share one aggregate projector so corruption and lifecycle semantics cannot diverge.
Failing the complete list on candidate corruption is safer than returning a plausible but incomplete control-plane view.
Pagination, indexes, and caching should follow measured history growth rather than precede it speculatively.
Discovery is read-only and grants no selection, transition, gate, action, execution, scheduling, provider, tool, or permission authority.
